texts.title_ja: キプリング「退却讃歌」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
God of our fathers, known of old,
Lord of our far-flung battle-line,
Beneath whose awful Hand we hold
Dominion over palm and pine

texts.title_original: Kipling - The Way Through the Woods
texts.title_ja: キプリング「森を抜ける道」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
They shut the road through the woods
Seventy years ago.
Weather and rain have undone it again,
And now you would never know

texts.title_ja: ハウスマン「最も美しき木」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Loveliest of trees, the cherry now
Is hung with bloom along the bough,
And stands about the woodland ride
Wearing white for Eastertide.

texts.title_ja: ハウスマン「私が二十一だった時」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
When I was one-and-twenty
I heard a wise man say,
'Give crowns and pounds and guineas
But not your heart away'

texts.title_original: Housman - To an Athlete Dying Young
texts.title_ja: ハウスマン「若くして死せる運動家へ」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
The time you won your town the race
We chaired you through the market-place;
Man and boy stood cheering by,
And home we brought you shoulder-high.

texts.title_ja: デ・ラ・メア「銀」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Slowly, silently, now the moon
Walks the night in her silver shoon;
This way, and that, she peers, and sees
Silver fruit upon silver trees

texts.title_ja: デ・ラ・メア「聴く者たち」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
'Is there anybody there?' said the Traveller,
Knocking on the moonlit door;
And his horse in the silence champed the grasses
Of the forest's ferny floor

texts.title_ja: エドワード・トマス「オールド・マン草」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Old Man, or Lad's-love,—in the name there's nothing
To one that knows not Lad's-love, or Old Man,
The hoar-green feathery herb, almost a tree

texts.title_ja: エドワード・トマス「消灯」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I have come to the borders of sleep,
The unfathomable deep
Forest where all must lose
Their way

texts.title_ja: オーウェン「奇妙な邂逅」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
It seemed that out of battle I escaped
Down some profound dull tunnel, long since scooped
Through granites which titanic wars had groined.

texts.title_ja: オーウェン「無益さ」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Move him into the sun—
Gently its touch awoke him once,
At home, whispering of fields half-sown.
Always it woke him, even in France

texts.title_ja: サスーン「みんな歌った」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Everyone suddenly burst out singing;
And I was filled with such delight
As prisoned birds must find in freedom,
Winging wildly across the white

texts.title_ja: ブルック「古き司祭館、グランチェスター」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Just now the lilac is in bloom,
All before my little room
And in my flower-beds, I think

texts.title_original: Rosenberg - Break of Day in the Trenches
texts.title_ja: ローゼンバーグ「塹壕の夜明け」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
The darkness crumbles away.
It is the same old druid Time as ever,
Only a live thing leaps my hand

texts.title_ja: グレンフェル「戦いへ」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
The naked earth is warm with spring,
And with green grass and bursting trees
Leans to the sun's gaze glorying,
And quivers in the sunny breeze

texts.title_ja: ビニヨン「斃れたる者へ」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
They shall grow not old, as we that are left grow old:
Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn.
At the going down of the sun and in the morning
We will remember them.

texts.title_ja: マクレー「フランドルの野に」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
In Flanders fields the poppies blow
Between the crosses, row on row,
That mark our place; and in the sky
The larks, still bravely singing, fly

texts.title_ja: チェスタトン「驢馬」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
When fishes flew and forests walked
And figs grew upon thorn,
Some moment when the moon was blood
Then surely I was born

texts.title_ja: イェイツ「君老いたるとき」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
When you are old and grey and full of sleep,
And nodding by the fire, take down this book,
And slowly read, and dream of the soft look
Your eyes had once

texts.title_original: Yeats - He Wishes for the Cloths of Heaven
texts.title_ja: イェイツ「天の衣を願う」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Had I the heavens' embroidered cloths,
Enwrought with golden and silver light,
The blue and the dim and the dark cloths
Of night and light and the half-light

texts.title_original: Yeats - A Prayer for My Daughter
texts.title_ja: イェイツ「我が娘のための祈り」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Once more the storm is howling, and half hid
Under this cradle-hood and coverlid
My child sleeps on. There is no obstacle
But Gregory's wood and one bare hill

texts.title_ja: イェイツ「クール湖の野生の白鳥」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
The trees are in their autumn beauty,
The woodland paths are dry,
Under the October twilight the water
Mirrors a still sky

texts.title_ja: エリオット「プルーフロック」'I have measured'
エリオット『荒地』「非現実の都市」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Unreal City,
Under the brown fog of a winter dawn,
A crowd flowed over London Bridge, so many,
I had not thought death had undone so many.

texts.title_ja: エリオット「東方の博士の旅」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
'A cold coming we had of it,
Just the worst time of the year
For a journey, and such a long journey:
The ways deep and the weather sharp'

texts.title_ja: パウンド「アルバ」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
As cool as the pale wet leaves
of lily-of-the-valley
She lay beside me in the dawn.

texts.title_ja: パウンド「商人の妻の手紙」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
While my hair was still cut straight across my forehead
I played about the front gate, pulling flowers.
You came by on bamboo stilts, playing horse,
You walked about my seat, playing with blue plums.

texts.title_original: Williams - This Is Just to Say
texts.title_ja: ウィリアムズ「ただ言いたいだけ」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I have eaten
the plums
that were in
the icebox

texts.title_ja: ウィリアムズ「赤い手押し車」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
so much depends
upon
a red wheel
barrow

texts.title_original: Stevens - Thirteen Ways of Looking at a Blackbird
texts.title_ja: スティーヴンス「黒鳥を見る13の方法」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Among twenty snowy mountains,
The only moving thing
Was the eye of the blackbird.

texts.title_ja: スティーヴンス「壺の逸話」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I placed a jar in Tennessee,
And round it was, upon a hill.
It made the slovenly wilderness
Surround that hill

texts.title_ja: H.D.「海の燕子花」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Weed, moss-weed,
root tangled in sand,
sea-iris, brittle flower

texts.title_ja: H.D.「オレアード」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Whirl up, sea—
whirl your pointed pines,
splash your great pines
on our rocks

texts.title_ja: ロレンス「蛇」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
A snake came to my water-trough
On a hot, hot day, and I in pyjamas for the heat,
To drink there.
In the deep, strange-scented shade of the great dark carob-tree

texts.title_ja: ロレンス「ピアノ」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Softly, in the dusk, a woman is singing to me;
Taking me back down the vista of years, till I see
A child sitting under the piano, in the boom of the tingling strings
And pressing the small, poised feet of a mother who smiles

texts.title_ja: フロスト「夜と知り合う」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I have been one acquainted with the night.
I have walked out in rain—and back in rain.
I have outwalked the furthest city light.
I have looked down the saddest city lane.

texts.title_ja: フロスト「デザイン」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I found a dimpled spider, fat and white,
On a white heal-all, holding up a moth
Like a white piece of rigid satin cloth—
Assorted characters of death and blight

texts.title_ja: フロスト「林檎を摘んだあと」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
My long two-pointed ladder's sticking through a tree
Toward heaven still,
And there's a barrel that I didn't fill
Beside it, and there may be two or three

texts.title_ja: ロビンソン「リチャード・コーリー」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Whenever Richard Cory went down town,
We people on the pavement looked at him:
He was a gentleman from sole to crown,
Clean favored, and imperially slim

texts.title_ja: ダンバー「我ら仮面を被る」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
We wear the mask that grins and lies,
It hides our cheeks and shades our eyes,—
This debt we pay to human guile;
With torn and bleeding hearts we smile

texts.title_ja: マッケイ「もし我ら死なねばならぬなら」
texts.era_period: ハーレム・ルネサンス
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
If we must die, let it not be like hogs
Hunted and penned in an inglorious spot,
While round us bark the mad and hungry dogs,
Making their mock at our accursed lot

texts.title_ja: マッケイ「ハーレムの影」
texts.era_period: ハーレム・ルネサンス
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I hear the halting footsteps of a lass
In Negro Harlem when the night lets fall
Its veil. I see the shapes of girls who pass

texts.title_original: Hughes - The Negro Speaks of Rivers
texts.title_ja: ヒューズ「黒人は河を語る」
texts.era_period: ハーレム・ルネサンス
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I've known rivers:
I've known rivers ancient as the world and older than the
   flow of human blood in human veins.
My soul has grown deep like the rivers.

texts.title_ja: ヒューズ「息子への母の言葉」
texts.era_period: ハーレム・ルネサンス
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Well, son, I'll tell you:
Life for me ain't been no crystal stair.
It's had tacks in it,
And splinters

texts.title_ja: カレン「それでも私は驚く」
texts.era_period: ハーレム・ルネサンス
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
I doubt not God is good, well-meaning, kind,
And did He stoop to quibble could tell why
The little buried mole continues blind,
Why flesh that mirrors Him must some day die

texts.title_original: Dickinson - The Soul has Bandaged Moments
texts.title_ja: ディキンソン「魂には繃帯された瞬間がある」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
The Soul has Bandaged moments –
When too appalled to stir –
She feels some ghastly Fright come up

texts.title_ja: ディキンソン「大いなる苦痛のあと」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
After great pain, a formal feeling comes –
The Nerves sit ceremonious, like Tombs –
The stiff Heart questions 'was it He, that bore,'

texts.title_ja: ディキンソン「真実をすべて語れ、しかし傾けて」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Tell all the truth but tell it slant —
Success in Circuit lies
Too bright for our infirm Delight
The Truth's superb surprise

texts.title_original: Whitman - When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard
texts.title_ja: ホイットマン「リラの花が前庭に最後に咲いた時」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
When lilacs last in the dooryard bloom'd,
And the great star early droop'd in the western sky in the night,
I mourn'd, and yet shall mourn with ever-returning spring.
Ever-returning spring, trinity sure to me you bring

texts.title_original: Whitman - Out of the Cradle Endlessly Rocking
texts.title_ja: ホイットマン「ゆりかごから出でて永遠に揺れる」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Out of the cradle endlessly rocking,
Out of the mocking-bird's throat, the musical shuttle,
Out of the Ninth-month midnight

texts.title_ja: ポー「アナベル・リー」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
It was many and many a year ago,
In a kingdom by the sea,
That a maiden there lived whom you may know
By the name of Annabel Lee

texts.title_ja: ポー「鐘」
texts.full_text_or_excerpt:
Hear the sledges with the bells—
Silver bells!
What a world of merriment their melody foretells!
How they tinkle, tinkle, tinkle
